chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Selling your property at the best price is no stroke of luck: it's the result of a method. The right starting price, preparation, marketing, negotiation and follow-up through to signing — every step counts.

This guide presents the 7-step game plan a broker uses to maximize the price and minimize stress. You'll know what to do, in what order, and why.

Each chapter ends with a lined « My notes » page to help you prepare YOUR sale.

chapters.title: Steps 1-2: the right price and preparation
chapters.objective: Start on the right footing: a fair price and a ready property.
chapters.html:
Start on the right footing: a fair price and a ready property.

Step 1 — Set the right price

The starting price is the most strategic decision. Too high, and the property stalls, goes stale on the market and ultimately sells for less; too low, and you leave money on the table. The price is set from a comparative market analysis (recent similar sales), not from wishful thinking.

Step 2 — Prepare the property

  • Declutter, deep-clean, depersonalize.
  • Minor repairs that jump out (handles, seals, touch-ups).
  • Light home staging to showcase the spaces (see the dedicated guide).
Emilie's tip

An overpriced property at the start almost always sells for less in the end: it becomes « the one that lingers ». The right price from day 1 creates the buzz that drives offers up.

chapters.title: Steps 3-4: marketing and showings
chapters.objective: Expose the property to the maximum number of qualified buyers.
chapters.html:
Expose the property to the maximum number of qualified buyers.

Step 3 — Market the property

  • Professional photos, video, a polished description (see the marketing guide).
  • Wide distribution (Centris, social media, broker network).
  • A complete and honest listing to attract the right buyers.

Step 4 — Manage the showings

Make showings easy (availability, constant cleanliness, owners absent). Every showing is an opportunity: a house that's hard to visit is a house that sells less well.

Emilie's tip

The first few weeks are the most important: that's when interest peaks. A well-prepared and well-priced property often generates its best offers early.

chapters.title: Steps 5-6: offers and negotiation
chapters.objective: Turn interest into the best accepted offer.
chapters.html:
Turn interest into the best accepted offer.

An offer is evaluated as a whole: price, conditions, dates, the strength of the buyer's financing. The highest isn't always the best if its conditions are shaky.

  • Analyze each offer: price, conditions (inspection, financing), deadlines.
  • Negotiate or make a counter-proposal while keeping your goal in mind.
  • In multiple offers, a structured strategy maximizes the result (see the dedicated guide).
Emilie's tip

Don't be dazzled by the number alone. A slightly lower offer that's condition-free and well-financed is sometimes safer — and more profitable — than a high but shaky one.

chapters.title: Step 7: from acceptance to closing
chapters.objective: Secure the sale through to signing.
chapters.html:
Secure the sale through to signing.

An accepted offer is not a completed sale: the conditions still have to be lifted (inspection, the buyer's financing, review of documents). Good follow-up keeps the transaction from derailing during this sensitive period.

  • Facilitate the inspection and access to the requested documents.
  • Provide the notary with the required documents (certificate of location, seller's declaration).
  • Prepare your own move and the handover of the keys.
Emilie's tip

Stay collaborative while the conditions are being lifted: a transaction well supported all the way to the notary is a transaction that reaches the finish line. That's where a broker's experience makes the difference.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Have a comparative analysis prepared to set the right price.
  2. Start decluttering and small repairs.

Within 30 days

  1. Carry out professional photos and marketing.
  2. Organize flexible, well-prepared showings.

Next

  1. Analyze the offers with Emilie and secure the transaction through to the notary.

chapters.title: Resources & glossary
chapters.html:
• Comparative market analysis: recent similar sales used to set the price.
  • Home staging: showcasing the property for the sale.
  • Marketing: photos, distribution and description to attract buyers.
  • Lifting the conditions: the period when the buyer validates inspection and financing.
  • Closing: signing the deed of sale at the notary's office.

qcm.q: The most strategic decision in a sale is:
options: A) The color of the sign
qcm.explanation: The right price creates the buzz (ch. 1).

qcm.q: An overpriced property at the start:
options: B) Often sells for less in the end
qcm.explanation: It becomes « the one that lingers » (ch. 1).

options: B) The first ones, when interest peaks
B) As a whole (price, conditions, dates, financing)
qcm.explanation: The highest isn't always the best (ch. 3).

options: B) Still subject to lifting the conditions
qcm.explanation: Inspection, financing and documents remain to be lifted (ch. 4).

qcm.q: While the conditions are being lifted, you should:
options: B) Stay collaborative and facilitate access

qcm.q: Making showings easy allows you to:
options: B) Expose the property to more buyers
qcm.explanation: A house that's easy to visit sells better (ch. 2).
